primitives.name: Neural Isomorphism Principle
primitives.verbatim_quote: only one other published report of a similar experience.\ It would seem that in such a case the neural process corresponding to the imagination must be the entire tract concerned in the actual sensation, even down as far as the retina.
primitives.assumptions: Neural pathways for sensation and imagination are structurally identical.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sensory input ceases, neural activity persists in same anatomical circuits.

layer2.mapping: Imaginative neural activity mirrors perceptual activity in spatial and temporal structure.
layer2.telemetry: fMRI or EEG correlation between perception and imagination states.

primitives.name: Sensory Persistence Law
primitives.verbatim_quote: The shock remaining in the ear and brain, after the sound of thunder, must pass through the same circles, and operate in the same way as during the actual sound.
primitives.assumptions: Post-stimulus neural activity follows same physical laws as during stimulation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: After stimulus removal, neural energy dissipates according to circuit resistance.

layer2.mapping: Persistence of sensory trace depends on residual neural excitation in recurrent pathways.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal decay profile of evoked potentials in auditory cortex.

primitives.name: Imagination Equivalence Postulate
primitives.verbatim_quote: With this single difference of intensity, the mode of existence of a sensation existing after the fact is essentially the same as its mode of existence during the fact.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I': 'intensity of imagination (dimensionless)', 'M': 'mode of neural activation (dimensionless)', 'F': 'function of neural firing (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Imagined sensations differ only in amplitude from real sensations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At zero intensity, imagination collapses to baseline neural noise.

layer2.mapping: Imaginal states are scaled versions of perceptual states under identical neural constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Comparative fMRI intensity maps of imagined vs. perceived stimuli.

This suggests a mathematical framework where sensory states form a vector space, and imagination corresponds to a scaled projection of that space. The persistence law implies a dynamical system governed by differential equations describing energy dissipation in neural networks. The isomorphism principle allows us to treat imagined and perceived states as equivalent elements in the same manifold, enabling probabilistic reasoning about mental states. Failure modes arise when neural circuits lack sufficient redundancy or when external interference disrupts the continuity of activation patterns.
